_comment: Golden vectors for ClimateController::evaluate() (src/Reptile.cpp). Single source of truth for both this repo's native test (test/test_climate) and the fleet webapp's reimplementation — see docs/automation-rules.md. All temp/hum values are Celsius/%RH, matching ClimateController's native units (and, since the wire-format change in CHANGELOG.md, what Supabase now stores). Each scenario replays its steps in order through ONE ClimateController instance — hysteresis is stateful, steps are not independent. The humidity-fault scenarios are stateful in a second way: the mist watchdog counts evaluations, so their step COUNT is load-bearing and not just the values.

steps.note: below tempLow -> heat on
above tempLow but inside hysteresis band -> stays on
reaches tempLow + 1.0 -> turns off
safety ceiling reached; fan reacts too
back below tempLow -> heat on again, fan releases
ceiling forces heat off immediately, no hysteresis on the way up
below humidityLow -> mist on
inside hysteresis band -> stays on
reaches humidityLow + 3.0 -> turns off
safety ceiling reached
back below humidityLow -> mist on again, fan releases
ceiling forces mist off immediately

scenarios.name: fan OR logic across independent triggers

steps.note: temperature-only trigger

humidity ceiling also hit -> both triggers active; this is the exact seam that caused the stale fan-reason bug fixed in firmware 0.4.1 (see CHANGELOG.md) - the fan itself doesn't flip here, only its cause changes
temp trigger releases, fan stays on for humidity alone
humidity trigger releases too -> fan off
evaluate() returns immediately when disabled, regardless of how extreme the reading is
below humidityLow -> mist on, sensor still trusted
0.0 %RH is not a dry enclosure, it is a dead channel -> fault latches, mist forced off
still zero -> stays latched; this is the runaway the gate exists to stop
still under HUMIDITY_PLAUSIBLE_MIN -> no recovery
plausible and risen above the 0.0 fault point -> trusted again, humidistat resumes

scenarios.name: humidity fault: mist watchdog on a plausible but dying channel

steps.note: below humidityLow -> mist on; the next step sets the watchdog baseline
watchdog baseline: 28.8 %RH
watchdog evaluation 2 of 2 — misting, yet the reading only falls
evaluation 3 exceeds MIST_NO_RISE_EVAL_LIMIT -> fault latches 60s of no-rise after the baseline, mist forced off
decaying further is more evidence of failure, not less -> stays latched (needs >= 29.4 to clear)
risen HUMIDITY_RISE_EPSILON above the 28.4 fault point -> trusted again, humidistat resumes

scenarios.name: humidity fault: suppresses the fan's humidity trigger only

steps.note: humidity ceiling -> fan on via the humidity trigger
channel dies -> humidity trigger dropped with it, fan releases
temperature is a separate channel -> fan still answers to heat while the fault stands
back under the temperature ceiling -> fan off, humidity still distrusted
below tempLow -> heat on, sensor still trusted
0 C is COLD, not broken — unlike 0 %RH it is a real reading, so no fault and the heater keeps working
below the SHT30's -40 C floor -> fault latches, heater forced off
still out of range -> stays latched
back inside the sensor's range -> trusted again, thermostat resumes and wants heat

scenarios.name: temperature fault: heater and temp trigger only, humidity untouched

steps.note: both ceilings -> fan on for both reasons, heat off, mist off
temperature channel dies -> temp trigger dropped, but the humidity ceiling still holds the fan on
humidity channel is untouched by a temperature fault -> mist resumes normally, fan releases
temperature back in range -> trusted again, heater resumes alongside the mister
